summary: Ground lookout between Jerome and Clarkdale with a 1938 cabin, staffed April to July; listed as gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone. No source found describes what, if anything, remains at the site.

events.note: William T. Anderson due on duty at a station between Jerome and Clarkdale
Left on duty when three of the forest's five lookouts were taken off
Fire lookout cabin near the highway between Clarkdale and Jerome; ground donated by a utility corporation
Verde station was the only one not manned, per an August 1949 report
A.R. Cannell was the fire lookout at the Verde station
Roadside fire below Jerome put out by Cannell and three men

evidence.supports: managed by Prescott National Forest, Yavapai County
1931 lookout due on duty at a station between Jerome and Clarkdale
evidence.quote: William T. Anderson will go on duty tomorrow morning as a lookout in the Verde district, at a station between Jerome and Clarkdale.

evidence.supports: 1933 three of five lookouts taken off because of rain; Verde lookout left on duty
evidence.quote: Because of the rain, Supervisor Frank Grubb of the Prescott national forest has taken off three of the five lookouts
That leaves the Verde valley lookout still on duty

evidence.supports: 1938 cabin completed near the highway between Clarkdale and Jerome
evidence.quote: The forest service has recently completed the construction of the fire look out cabin near the highway between Clarkdale and Jerome.

evidence.supports: ground donated by a utility corporation
evidence.quote: The ground was donated by the Upper Verde Public Utilities corporation.
A lookout is being maintained in this location from April 1 to July 31.

evidence.supports: August 1949 Verde station the only one not manned
evidence.quote: The Verde valley lookout station is the only one that is not manned at this time.

evidence.supports: April 1950 Cannell at Verde station spotted fire below Jerome
evidence.quote: Last Thursday A.R. Cannell, fire lookout at the Verde station, spotted a fire on the edge of the highway below Jerome.

evidence.supports: Cannell and three men put the fire out
evidence.quote: Cannell, with three men, went to the fire and extinguished it with Indian pumps and fire fighting tools.

evidence.supports: no source describes the site today (listing shows gone)

notes_for_editor: The 1931-1950 history comes from newspaper excerpts (Prescott Evening Courier, as quoted by a hobby site); the originals were not read. No source gives a removal date or cause for the cabin. The 1931 station and the 1938 cabin are both described between Jerome and Clarkdale; the sources do not say whether they are the same spot. The ground was donated by a utility corporation; current ownership and access were not checked. The Peakbagging list also places a Verde Valley (LO site) at Clarkdale but was not used.
